purpose: A parlay or prop combo is a joint probability. This table separates three states that are usually confused: dependence that is exact by construction (nested events), dependence with a known sign but unknown size, and dependence that we have not measured. The third state is where every row in the 'measured' column currently sits, and the gate (G-11) forbids pricing through it.
measured_column_rule: The measured column is blank for every non-nested pair because this repository contains no resolved tickets. A blank here is the correct output of the verification policy, not a gap to fill in.

pairs.legs: Same player: over 4.5 receptions AND over 3.5 receptions
pairs.relation: same game, same player, monotonic ladder
pairs.rho: EXACT: A (higher line) implies B, so P(A and B) = P(A) and the correlation is determined by the two marginal probabilities alone
pairs.handling: Never parlay a nested pair: the joint carries no more information than the tighter leg, and multiplying marginals would understate dependence to the point of nonsense.

pairs.relation: same game, same team, monotonic ladder
pairs.rho: EXACT by the same identity as C-01
pairs.handling: Eligible only as a single-leg bet at the chosen line; operators commonly refuse same-ladder parlays.

pairs.legs: Game total over 47.5 AND team A team total over 24.5
pairs.handling: Requires a fitted joint scoring model (ST-02); the marginal product is a systematic overstatement of the ticket's chance because both legs ride the same pace.

pairs.legs: Team A team total over AND A's starting RB rush yards over
pairs.handling: This is the classic 'structural correlation' operators build SGP prices around; enter only with a fitted dependence (ST-10).

pairs.legs: A player's receptions over AND the same player's receiving yards over
pairs.relation: same game, same player, two views of one volume variable
pairs.handling: Price from one latent distribution (ST-12) and require the model to reproduce both single-prop prices as a self-consistency check.

pairs.legs: Team A spread -3 AND Team B moneyline (opponents)
pairs.direction: negative (near-deterministic, but not exactly: a -3 spread and a moneyline differ on margins of 1-3)
pairs.handling: Near-complementary; operators void such combinations, and any residual dependence is a push/margin-definition artefact rather than an edge.

pairs.legs: Two different games on the same Sunday (both overs)
pairs.direction: small positive expected (league-wide pace, weather patterns, shared rules)
pairs.handling: Default to independence for logging, but the ticket may only be funded once our own measured dependence excludes zero at the registered level (ST-11).

pairs.legs: Two legs from games sharing a common opponent or a divisional rematch within a week
pairs.handling: Treated like C-07 but flagged SHARED-CONTEXT; it is the residue 'independence' hides in cross-game parlays.

pairs.legs: Same game: over 47.5 AND the other team's pass attempts over
pairs.handling: Requires the pace component of the joint model; do not price with an at-bat independence assumption.

pairs.legs: Same game: both starting QBs' completion overs
pairs.relation: same game, competing units with a shared total
pairs.direction: near zero to slightly negative (a tight, low-event game limits both; a fast game inflates both)
pairs.handling: Sign cannot be asserted without measurement; log and measure, never assume independence for funding.

pairs.legs: Anytime TD scorer AND that player's team winning
pairs.handling: The most commonly boosted SGP pair in the market; precisely because the boost under-charges it. Needs measurement before any use.

pairs.legs: Player prop legs for two players on the same team who share touches (two RBs' rush-yard overs)
pairs.relation: same game, same backfield, competing for a fixed resource
pairs.direction: negative (workload substitution), which most parlay pricing ignores
pairs.handling: The negative dependence means the naive product of marginals OVERSTATES the ticket's value; the classic SGP trap on a 'both RBs over' ticket.

pairs.legs: Same game: team A win AND team A kicker field goals made over
pairs.relation: same game, conditional on drives and substitutions
pairs.handling: Coach-specific pull patterns make this a poor first measurement target; park it.

pairs.legs: Any two legs across different weeks of a season-long parlay
pairs.handling: Even here, the outcome distribution is not independent of the same roster-injury and schedule contexts our availability model reads; treat 'independent' as a modelling assumption with a name, not as a fact.

method.estimator: Pearson correlation of binary outcomes across our own resolved tickets, reported with a season-block bootstrap interval; for continuous prop pairs, correlation of realised values against projections (residual correlation), which is what a joint pricing model actually needs.
method.bounds: Where no estimate exists, the only defensible statement is the Fréchet-Hoeffding bound on the joint probability implied by the two marginals; the builder computes the corresponding correlation bounds so the reader can see how useless they are for pricing (see the bounds table on this page).
method.why_not_import: A published correlation from another operator, another season or another scoring rule is not our measurement: it does not come with our marginals, our cut-off or our settlement definitions, and the site's own verification rule forbids laundering it into a verified row.
method.minimum_n_per_pair: At least 300 resolved tickets per pair before a measured value may be used in a price, and only if the bootstrap interval excludes the operator's implied value at the registered level.
